findings.claim: §Error Messages states that the existing export `TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic.forbidden` carries the text "You do not have permission to do that." and marks the row `New: no`. The export carries "You do not have permission to manage templates", and that is the string every `CapabilityGuard` refusal in the product already puts on the wire — so a manager refused the portal's settings reads a sentence about templates, and the only way to make the spec's text true changes a message four other areas emit and breaks two shipped tests the spec's own README promises are untouched.

witness.detail: specs/portal/01-home.contracts.md §Error Messages: '| `TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic.forbidden` | `GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/portal/settings`, `PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/portal/settings` | You do not have permission to do that. | no |'. The code: packages/validation/src/documents.ts:125 reads `forbidden: 'You do not have permission to manage templates',` inside `TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic` (the object is declared at documents.ts:64 and there is exactly one), and apps/api/src/auth/capability.guard.ts:63-66 raises `new ForbiddenException({ error: 'forbidden', message: TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic.forbidden })`. Scenario: a `manager` of the organization calls `PUT /api/organizations/{orgId}/portal/settings` with a valid body. §Routes names `CapabilityGuard('ManagePortalSettings')` on that route, so the guard refuses with 403 and the body's message is 'You do not have permission to manage templates' — not the sentence §Error Messages states. The two implementations that could satisfy the row instead: (1) change the export's text, which alters the 403 message of every `@RequireCapability` route in documents, hiring, clients, holidays, reports and requests, and fails `apps/api/test/document-templates.spec.ts:576` (`message: 'You do not have permission to manage templates'`) and `packages/validation/src/documents.test.ts`, both of which assert the literal — while specs/portal/README.md §Blast Radius says 'Nothing in the documents, hiring, requests, reports or time-off areas changes' and §Backward Compatibility says 'Every existing route answers exactly what it answered'; (2) emit a portal-owned message instead, which requires raising the refusal in the service rather than by the guard — the pattern requests/02 already uses for `REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.manageForbidden` (packages/validation/src/roles.ts:98-101) — and contradicts the `CapabilityGuard('ManagePortalSettings')` the §Routes table names on both settings routes. No implementation satisfies the Error Messages row, the Routes row and the README's two guarantees together.

findings.suggestedFix: One decision, in this spec's own text. Either correct the row to the text the export actually carries and accept that a portal refusal says 'templates' — in which case say so deliberately, because it is a sentence a manager reads on a portal screen — or give the portal its own `PORTAL_MESSAGES.settingsForbidden`, mark the row `New: yes`, and change the §Routes Guards column on both settings rows from `CapabilityGuard('ManagePortalSettings')` to a capability check in the service, which is where this repository already raises a refusal whose message a spec names. The third answer — rewording `TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic.forbidden` itself to a generic sentence — is a real product improvement and is a change to five other areas, so it belongs in a document of its own rather than inside this one; if it is taken here, the README's 'Nothing in the documents … areas changes' and 'Every existing route answers exactly what it answered' must both go, and the two shipped assertions of the old literal must be named as amended.
